Name: Maghreb Spice Mix
Short description: The North African chilli paste behind Maghreb cooking: dried red chillies, garlic, lemon, cumin, coriander, and caraway.
Description: How to Make the Dish: Harissa lives all over Maghrebi cooking - stirred into couscous broth, spooned into shakshuka's tomato-and-pepper sauce, or rubbed onto merguez sausages before they hit the grill. From Episode 5 of the Fudi People YouTube series. WET - a chilli paste, not a dry blend; needs refrigeration after opening, not a shelf-stable pantry jar as scripted.

Name: West Africa Spice Mix
Short description: The dry suya rub behind Ghana and Nigeria's chinchinga and suya: grains of selim, dried chillies, kuli-kuli (peanut puffs), ginger, and a stock cube.
Description: How to Make the Dish: Skewer beef or chicken, rub generously with Yaji, and grill over an open flame until charred - suya, West Africa's best-known street food. Yaji also seasons kilishi (dried spiced beef jerky) and gets dusted straight onto roasted plantain, corn, or boiled eggs. From Episode 1 of the Fudi People YouTube series. Dry blend, shelf-stable. Contains peanuts (kuli-kuli); may contain gluten depending on the stock cube used. Note: West Africa also has two other drafted blends not otherwise placed in this structure - Senegal's Yassa Marinade (Episode 2) and Sierra Leone/Liberia's Pepper Soup Spice (Episode 4) - worth a look as future variations or separate listings.

Njangsa on its own also gives ndole, Cameroon's national dish, its bitter-greens depth. From Episode 7 of the Fudi People YouTube series. WET - ground with fresh garlic and onion, this comes out a moist paste rather than a dry rub; a dry version would need onion and garlic powder substituted in. May contain peanuts if using the peanut substitute for njangsa.
